key_insight: The Asta Interaction Dataset provides the first large-scale, real-world view of how researchers use LLM-powered literature discovery and question-answering tools, revealing diverse query intents, iterative search behaviors, and varying reliance on retrieved sources versus generated summaries.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of empirical evidence about real researcher interactions with deployed AI-powered scientific tools, limiting principled design, evaluation, and alignment of such systems to practitioner needs.
method: Collected and released >200,000 anonymized user queries and interaction logs from two deployed tools within an LLM-powered retrieval-augmented platform (literature discovery and scientific QA).
Characterized usage patterns via quantitative analyses (query types, session length, click/engagement rates, iterative refinements) and qualitative inspection of representative interactions.
Compared behaviors across tools to surface differences in intent, trust in generated answers, and reliance on retrieved documents to inform design recommendations.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners, HCI researchers, and tool builders to ground design decisions and evaluation metrics in real-world researcher behavior, improving retrieval, explanation, and UI choices for scientific workflows.
visual_elements: Stacked bar chart of query intent distribution (e.g., discovery vs. direct QA vs. follow-up refinement).
Session funnel diagram showing drop-off and engagement at stages (query → view retrieved docs → accept/generated answer → follow-up query).
Sankey diagram linking initial intents to final outcomes (satisfaction, follow-up, document clicks) to illustrate iterative behavior.
Heatmap/time-series of query volume and engagement across research stages or time-of-day to show usage patterns
paper_title: Understanding Usage and Engagement in AI-Powered Scientific Research Tools: The Asta Interaction Dataset
paper_authors: Dany Haddad, Dan Bareket, Joseph Chee Chang, Jay DeYoung, Jena D. Hwang
